context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Thomas Tiffany (R) did not seek re-election to this district in 2026. Fred Clark defeated Ginger Murray and Chris Armstrong in the Democratic primary. Michael Alfonso defeated Kevin Hermening, Jessi Ebben, Niina Threlfall-Baum, and Donald Raihala in the Republican primary.

candidates.name: Fred Clark
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Ginger Murray and Chris Armstrong in the Democratic primary.
candidates.currentRole: Owner, Clark Forestry, Inc.; former Wisconsin State Assembly member

summary.text: Fred Clark is the Democratic nominee for the open 7th District. A forester and small-business owner, he served in the Wisconsin State Assembly from 2009 to 2015 and has served on state conservation and tourism bodies. He is running for Congress after relocating to Bayfield County.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Michigan State University in 1985 and a master's degree from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992.

Has worked as a forester and land manager: a service forester/consultant with the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, a forest ecologist for The Nature Conservancy, and owner of Clark Forestry, Inc.
Elected to the Wisconsin State Assembly and represented District 81 from 2009 to 2015; in 2009-2010 he was vice chair of the Forestry committee and of Tourism, Recreation and State Properties.
In 2011 he ran in a recall election against Republican state Sen. Luther Olsen in Senate District 14 and lost, 52.1% to 47.8%; he won re-election to the Assembly in 2012.

Has served on the Wisconsin Council on Forestry, the Wisconsin Council on Tourism and the state Natural Resources Board, and provides forestry management consulting services, according to UpNorthNews.
A Democrat from Bayfield, he said in 2025 that he has been involved in conservation and environmental policy and community volunteering in Bayfield County since leaving the legislature.
Announced his candidacy on October 1, 2025, after incumbent Tom Tiffany decided to run for governor; won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary with 37.5% over Ginger Murray and Chris Armstrong.

priorities.text: Says elected representatives should represent everyone, not billionaires and elites whose influence he says captures politicians of both parties, and calls for setting aside old partisanship.
Says he is personally passionate about conservation, public lands, small businesses, and Congressional oversight.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he would support protecting and expanding Medicare and Medicaid and providing a public health care option available to everyone.
positions.quote: Providing a public health care option available for everyone.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he would support passage of the Women’s Health Protection Act to create a legal protection for the right to provide and access abortion.
positions.quote: Passage of the Women’s Health Protection Act, creating a new legal protection for the right to provide and access abortion, free from medically unnecessary restrictions and bans.

positions.summary: His campaign site criticizes quota-driven mass deportations and the planned growth of ICE, and says he would focus enforcement on violent criminals while still supporting deportation of criminals.
positions.quote: Focusing immigration enforcement on keeping violent criminals off of our streets, not harassing legal immigrants while executing mass, quota-driven deportations.

positions.summary: His campaign plan calls for a tax code in which the wealthiest individuals and corporations pay their share, and for tax reform that reverses past tax cuts for the wealthiest Americans and most profitable corporations.
positions.quote: We need a fair tax code that ensures everybody pays their share, including the wealthiest individuals and corporations.

record.text: Served on the Wisconsin Assembly's Education, Environment and Forestry, Jobs Economy and Mining, and Natural Resources and Sporting Heritage committees during the 2013-2014 legislative session.
Voted no on Assembly Bill 11, January 2011 Special Session (2011 Wisconsin Act 10, eliminating most collective bargaining for public employees), which the Assembly concurred in 53-42 on 2011-03-10.
Voted yes on SB 93 (allowing concealed carry of firearms with a permit), which the Assembly concurred in 68-27 on 2011-06-21.
Voted no on AB 7 (requiring photo identification to vote), which passed the Assembly 60-35 on 2011-05-11.

candidates.researchNotes: Clark's Assembly service is given as 2009 to 2015 per Ballotpedia; no campaign website was located in the sources reviewed.

candidates.name: Michael Alfonso
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Kevin Hermening, Jessi Ebben, Niina Threlfall-Baum, and Donald Raihala in the Republican primary.

summary.text: Michael Alfonso is the Republican nominee for the open 7th District. He says he was raised in Vilas County and Wausau, studied mathematics at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, worked in construction and concrete, and produced The Dan Bongino Show podcast. He has not held elected office; he won the August 2026 Republican primary with President Trump's endorsement.

background.text: According to his campaign website, raised in Vilas County and Wausau, Wisconsin; his grandparents fled Cuba at the end of the Castro Revolution.
Paid his own way through the University of Wisconsin-Madison by working in construction, and earned a Bachelor of Science in mathematics.
Married Evita Duffy at 22 and began married life in Hayward, Wisconsin, returning to the construction and concrete industry; per his campaign website.
About a year later became producer of The Dan Bongino Show podcast, according to his campaign website.
Has not held elected office. Endorsed by President Trump in the Republican primary; his father-in-law, Sean Duffy, held the 7th District seat until 2019.
Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary with 48.9% of the vote over Kevin Hermening and others; if elected, he would be the youngest member of Congress, according to WXPR.

priorities.text: "Michael Alfonso will support school choice, boost homeschooling protections, and end Marxist race and gender indoctrination in classrooms."
"Michael Alfonso will fight to ban members of Congress from trading stocks."
"Michael Alfonso will lower costs, increase transparency, and prioritize patients"

positions.summary: His campaign site says he backs constitutional carry and will protect the Second Amendment against attempts to weaken it.
positions.quote: He backs constitutional carry and our right to defend ourselves.

positions.summary: His campaign site describes him as pro-life from conception, praises the overturning of Roe v. Wade so states can protect the unborn, and says he opposes expanding mail-in abortion pills.
positions.quote: Like our Founding Fathers, Michael believes every person has an inherent right to life—from conception to natural death.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he will support school choice.
positions.quote: Michael Alfonso will support school choice, boost homeschooling protections

candidates.researchNotes: Statements come from his campaign Issues page. No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey or debate coverage was reviewed; his page does not address tariffs, minimum wage, taxes, climate, police funding or rent. Alfonso has a campaign website with a 'Meet Michael' page and issues page, but he has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his biography relies mainly on his own materials.
